what_it_does: When multiple virtual machines (VMs) share the same physical memory chip, one VM can sometimes spy on another by carefully timing how long its own memory requests take — a subtle attack called a timing side-channel. One defense is to give each VM a fixed time slot on the memory bus regardless of whether it has requests ready, so the timing pattern reveals nothing about what the other VM is doing. The problem is that these fixed slots must be sized for the worst case (a mix of slow write operations and fast read operations), so most slots are wasted, roughly halving memory throughput. FlexProf introduces two flavors of time slot: one sized for mostly-read traffic and one sized for mostly-write traffic. A coarse-grained profiler — one that deliberately avoids learning fine-grained details that would itself become a privacy leak — observes each VM's read-versus-write ratio and assigns the appropriate slot type. Within each slot, spare capacity can be opportunistically used for the other operation type, recovering throughput while keeping the rigid fixed-slot structure that prevents information from leaking between VMs.
